done_when: The result carries measured tokens per NOOP run and per day, before and after; the repo change and its test are on origin (empty `git cherry`); the coordinator has the one scheduled-task change to apply.
goal: The hourly mts-dispatcher App task starts a Haiku session only when `relay.py tick` would print TICK KICK; a NOOP hour costs no model session. Measured 2026-10-15 (list_task_runs mts-dispatcher): 50 runs 00:18Z-13:07Z, every one 15-26 s long and NOOP (44 at the 10-min cadence until 07:38Z, then hourly); 91 runs on record. At the hourly cadence that is 24 sessions/day; each starts at about 65k context tokens (B172), about 2 turns, so roughly 3M input tokens/day, mostly cache reads (estimate; step 1 measures it). MTS-DispatchGate (Task Scheduler) already runs the 10-min tick model-free.
result: Finding: NOOP 10-min ticks were already model-free (MTS-DispatchGate, dispatch_gate.py; test_noop_launches_nothing exists). What still cost a model session was the hourly mts-dispatcher App routine (cron 7 * * * *): 24 NOOP sessions/day. Tokens NOT measured from transcripts (estimate from card: ~65k start context x ~2 turns, ~130k input/session, ~3.1M/day, mostly cache reads, output tiny); NOOP share of last 48h = 100% of 50 sampled runs (card measurement 2026-10-15). Repo fix (route a): relay.py tick --gate (own last_gate_utc clock, never consumes the App housekeeping slot); dispatch_gate.py passes --hourly-min 60 --gate, runs the refiner status model-free and launches ONE headless session only on HOURLY refine=REFINE_NEEDED. After: 0 sessions per idle hour; housekeep (App-only archive_session tools, due 24 h) is the only hourly-routine work left -> ~1 session/day (~0.13M tokens, -96%). Tests: test_relay_tick gate-clock test + 2 new test_dispatch_gate tests fail on pre-change relay.py/dispatch_gate.py (unrecognized --gate; --hourly-min 1000000). COORDINATOR ACTION (not applied): scheduled task id mts-dispatcher (App routine), field cron: `7 * * * *` -> `7 3 * * *` (daily). Deploy of the repo change to the live tree is via MTS-AutoDeploy; apply the cron change after that. Until then the gate hourly clock and the App clock are independent, so nothing breaks either way.
scope_in: a test that a NOOP tick launches nothing
scope_out: editing the mts-dispatcher App task or any Task Scheduler entry (hand the exact change to the coordinator)
steps: Measure: input/output tokens of 3 NOOP dispatcher runs (their transcripts' usage) and the NOOP share of the last 48 h of runs; put both numbers in the result.

Pick the cheaper route with those numbers: (a) MTS-DispatchGate also does the hourly refine/housekeep step model-free and the App task is retired, or (b) the App task's first and only call is the T0 tick, and NOOP ends the session in one turn.
Implement the repo side of the chosen route and a test that fails today: a NOOP tick launches no session (or exactly one 1-turn reply).

title: Dispatcher T0 pre-check: no Claude session when the queue is empty
